newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 12.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett has taken the lead in a joint announcement with Federal Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith which will see Victoria hand over its industrial relations powers to the Commonwealth. The new arrangement will streamline Vicoria's industrial relations system whilst allowing businesses to avoid dual regulation under State and Federal legislation. Page 1.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels has called for the removal of a number of foreign ownership restrictions on local media, claiming the current rules limit global competition and restrict diversity. The ACCC's view has bee backed by major media groups, including newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings and the Ten Network. Page 1.

Former Prime Minister Paul Keating has re-entered the political landscape in a speech condemning Prime Minister John Howard for lack of leadership in the current race debate. Keating made renewed calls for Australia to play a stronger role in the Asian region as he lashed out at current attacks on the policy of multiculturalism. Page 2.

President of the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Graeme Samuel, has called on the Howard Government to reform the taxation system to relieve current compliance burden on small business, identified by the Small Business Deregulation Task Force The ACCI call came as Prime Minister John Howard rejected the move for tax reform in the current climate, claiming the issue did not have universal support. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a move which will result in wage agreements registered under the Victorian Government's controversial industrial relations laws being phased out, State Premier Jeff Kennett yesterday agreed to a transfer of State industrial relations powers to the Commnwealth - making it the first such voluntary transfer since Federation. Page 1.

Appearing for his second lecture as a visiting professor at the University of New South Wales in Sydney, former Prime Minister Paul Keating described the race debate as a great tragedy which had harmed Australia's reputation. Keating also made a strong inirect attack on Prime Minister John Howard for not standing up to Independent MP Pauline Hanson's controversial politics. Page 1.

Governor-General Sir William Deane and Prime Minister John Howard observed the traditional Remembrance Day pause for silence on the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month to mark the end of hostilities along the Western Front in 1918, along with a small crowd outside the Australian War Memorial in Canberra yesterday. Page 1.

In a rebuff to the Federal Government, the nation's competition watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, has called for the abolition of the "arbitrary" restrictions on foreign ownership of Australian media, saying any reform to mediaownership policy would be undermined if the foreign ownership limits were left unchanged. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As part of a huge shake-up of the New South Wales police force recommended in an interim report by Police Royal Commissioner Justice Wood, the State Police Board is to be scrapped and its functions transferred to Peter Ryan, making him the most powerful Plice Commissioner in New South Wales history. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday described a deal which will see Victoria transferring its industrial relations powers to the Commonwealth as a victory for a new era of "pragmatic federalism". The Federal Government is hoping the move will put pressure on other States to follow suit so that it can achieve its long-term goal of assuming complete control of industrial relations. Page 1.

In a stinging attack on the Howard Government's decision to cut legal aid funding to the States, New South Wales' most senior law officer, Director of Public Prosecutions Nicholas Cowdery QC, warned yesterday attempts to intimidate and pay off criminal trial jurors to encourage hung juries may rise because of the cutbacks. Page 1.

The Seven Network's current affairs show Witness will return next year, but without its executive producer Peter Manning, who from today, will oversee the development of the Network's public affairs programs after apparently losing a battle with Witness host Jana Wendt over claims he had taken the program downmarket. Page 1.
THE AGE

In what is being dubbed a historic deal, Victoria will hand over its industrial relations powers to the Federal Government, with the aim of ending duplication for workers. Following the joint announcement by Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett and Federal Indutrial Relations Minister Peter Reith, all of the State's workers will have access to Commonwealth awards and unfair dismissal laws. Page A1.

The Malaysian Deputy Opposition Leader, Lim Guan Eng, has slammed Prime Minister John Howard over his lack of criticism regarding the weekend's conference on East Timor, which was marred by violent disruptions and the subsequent deportation of the Australan delegates from Malaysia. The Malaysian Opposition feels many would be disgusted by Howard's refusal to defend democracy and free speech. Page A1.

A chocolate dessert sauce produced by a Cairns company is believed to be responsible for an outbreak of food poisoning among Qantas passengers to Japan and Taiwan. Over 100 passengers on eight flights last week were affected as the Australian airline now aces a public relations disaster in the competitive Japanese market. Page A2.

Renewed fears of a "superbug" which is resistant to powerful drugs have surfaced again in Australian hospitals following the death of an elderly woman early this month at the Austin Medical Centre. Tests conducted on the woman after she died as a result of liver failure revealed the bacterium Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus was present in her bowel. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
